newsitem.title: POLAND: EAST EUROPEAN POLICE BRAINSTORM ON BEATING CRIME.
newsitem.headline: EAST EUROPEAN POLICE BRAINSTORM ON BEATING CRIME.

text.p: East European police officers, swapping ideas in Poland on how cooperate in fighting crime and the drugs trade, said on Thursday they had already scored major successes as a result of such annual conferences.

Russia's police liaison officer in Warsaw, Anatoly Gulkov, said the meetings had led to the arrest of eight gang members making drugs in Poland and a man in St Petersburg who had defrauded large sums from banks, PAP news agency reported.

The three-day fifth International Conference of Criminal Police at Legionowo near Warsaw was attended by delegates from Belarus, Lithuania, Latvia, Moldavia, Russia, Ukraine, Slovakia and Hungary, with French and Dutch liaison officers present.
Some kinds of serious, organised crime including narcotics are flourishing in the countries and ex-satellites of the former Soviet Union.
Western Europe shares concern, especially as states including Poland approach membership of the European Union which could ease the westward flow of cross-border crime.
Poland is about to introduce visa-free travel with Russia, and has relaxed borders with other ex-Soviet neighbours.
Polish police chief Jerzy Stanczyk said cross-border crime could not be controlled by artificially restricting travel.
"International crime can be stemmed by good international cooperation between the anti-criminal services," PAP reported him as saying.
The officers resolved to step up action against narcotics, fight armed highway robbery and establish principles for passing on advance intelligence on movements of dangerous criminals, it said.
Stanczyk said Poland and Ukraine had experimentally exchanged police databases on crime.
Police representatives said the global rising crime trend had been braked in their countries, PAP reported.
But new forms had emerged in recent years including killing for hire, a greatly increased drugs trade, illegal immigration and a booming business in the theft and smuggling of cars.
